nws.label: US weather from the National Weather Service
nws.termsRead: 2026-10-31: open data, free to use for any purpose; a User-Agent is required; rate limits exist but aren't published.
nws.attribution: Weather from the National Weather Service

paths.does: The forecast office and grid square for a US place, by latitude and longitude (4 decimals at most). Its properties.forecast link is the forecast path.
The 7-day forecast for a grid square, in 12-hour periods.
The hourly forecast for a grid square.
Active weather alerts for a state (area=KS) or a point (point=38.89,-77.03).

wikipedia.label: Wikipedia article summaries and search (English)
wikipedia.termsRead: 2026-10-31: no key; an informative User-Agent with contact is required; no hard read limit, requests in series, cache what can be reused. Text is CC BY-SA 4.0, so a product shows where it came from.
wikipedia.attribution: From Wikipedia, under CC BY-SA 4.0, with a link to the article

paths.does: One article's title, short description, first paragraph (extract), thumbnail and link (content_urls.desktop.page). Title with underscores for spaces.
Articles matching words (q), up to 20 (limit), each with its key, title and excerpt.

openlibrary.label: Open Library book search and records
openlibrary.termsRead: 2026-10-31: no key; identify the app in the User-Agent; 3 requests a second when identified; no bulk downloads (the gateway's cache and daily cap keep products far from that).

paths.does: Books matching q, title or author, up to 20 a page (limit, page). Pass fields (key,title,author_name,first_publish_year,cover_i) to keep the answer small. A cover is https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/<cover_i>-M.jpg.
One work's record by its key, like OL27482W: title, description, subjects.

usgs.label: Earthquakes from the US Geological Survey
usgs.termsRead: 2026-10-31: USGS data is US public domain; credit is asked for ("U.S. Geological Survey").

paths.does: Earthquakes as GeoJSON features (properties.mag, place, time, url), by dates (starttime, endtime as YYYY-MM-DD), minmagnitude, a circle (latitude, longitude, maxradiuskm), limit up to 100 and orderby.
A ready-made list: significant, 4.5, 2.5, 1.0 or all, over the past hour, day, week or month (like significant_week).
